results.title: AI Ethics Education in India: A Syllabus-Level Review of Computing Courses
results.content: # AI Ethics Education in India: A Syllabus-Level Review of Computing Courses. The pervasive integration of artificial intelligence (AI) across domains such as healthcare, governance, finance, and education has intensified scrutiny of its ethical implications, including algorithmic bias, privacy risks, accountability, and societal impact. This study addresses that gap through a large-scale analysis of 3,395 publicly accessible syllabi from CS and allied areas at leading Indian institutions. Three key findings emerged: (1) AI ethics is typically integrated as a minor module within broader technical courses rather than as a standalone course; (2) ethics coverage is often limited to just one or two instructional sessions; and (3) recurring topics include algorithmic fairness, privacy and data governance, transparency, and societal impact. This work highlights both the progress and the gaps in preparing future technologists to engage meaningfully with the ethical dimensions of AI, and it offers suggestions to strengthen the integration of AI ethics within computing curricula.

results.title: Scientist Personality: Traits, Types, and Career Impact
results.content: Scientist Personality: Traits, Types, and Career Implications. Curiosity and logic may be the hallmarks of scientific thinking, but the minds behind groundbreaking discoveries are far more diverse and complex than the stereotypical lab-coat-wearing genius. The world of science is populated by a rich tapestry of personalities, each contributing their unique strengths and perspectives to the pursuit of knowledge. From the meticulous data analyst to the visionary theorist, the realm of scientific inquiry embraces a wide spectrum of intellectual and emotional traits. The investigative personality that drives scientific progress is a multifaceted gem, reflecting different facets depending on the individual and their chosen field of study. ## Unraveling the Scientist Personality: A Tapestry of Traits. This curious personality is the engine that propels scientific inquiry forward, constantly asking “why” and “how” in the face of the unknown. It’s this relentless pursuit of understanding that has led to some of humanity’s greatest discoveries and innovations.

results.title: The role of personality traits in predicting educational use of generative AI in higher education | Scientific Reports
results.content:
Title: The role of personality traits in predicting educational use of generative AI in higher education | Scientific Reports
Studying the effects of personality traits on the use of Gen-AI is crucial for understanding the role of individual differences in integrating this innovative technology into education. Therefore, this study investigated how the Big Five personality traits, age, and gender predict the educational use of Gen-AI in higher education. These findings significantly advance our understanding of the relationship between personality traits and the use of Gen-AI in higher education. Based on the literature, a noticeable gap exists regarding research dedicated to exploring the role of personality traits in predicting students’ use of Gen-AI for educational purposes. Unlike traditional educational technologies, Gen-AI can generate content and support creativity; therefore, individuals’ personality traits, particularly openness to innovation and conscientiousness, may play a decisive role in the use of Gen-AI. This study aims to explore the role of the “Big Five Personality Traits,” also known as the “Five Factor Model” (FFM), in predicting students’ use of Gen-AI for educational purposes. Thus, this study aims to address this gap by investigating the significance of these personality traits in predicting students’ use of Gen-AI within academic contexts. Nevertheless, existing studies have not explicitly explored how personality traits may impact students’ use of Gen-AI in educational settings. The findings shed light on the considerable connections between four personality traits and the educational use of Gen-AI, aligning with prior literature that emphasizes the substantial impact of the “Big Five personality traits” on the adoption of emerging technologies21."). The outcomes established a significant relationship between certain personality traits and the educational use of Gen-AI among undergraduate students. The personality trait of agreeableness did not indicate a significant relationship with the educational use of Gen-AI. Finally, the findings of the multi-group analysis reveal gender differences in how personality traits predict educational use of Gen-AI. The ANN-based sensitivity analysis provided more profound insights into the relative importance of personality traits in predicting the educational use of Gen-AI. The results show that personality traits, such as openness and a sense of responsibility, are strong determinants of the educational use of Gen-AI technologies. The findings revealed the key role of certain personality traits in predicting educational use of Gen-AI.
